Answer: B
Reason: The coronal CT reconstruction (Figure 6) demonstrates massive dilatation of the trachea and main bronchi, which is the hallmark of Mounier-Kuhn syndrome. The axial CT images (Figures 4 and 5) show extensive cystic spaces (representing severe bronchiectasis/tracheobronchomegaly) that communicate with the airways, along with some fluid levels, consistent with this diagnosis.
